claims.statement: Galpi spans three runtimes (TypeScript webview, Rust/Tauri host, Python sidecar) that all follow one dependency rule: dependencies point inward to domain; ports are owned by the consuming inner layer and implemented by adapters; framework code (Tauri, Zod, CPAL, tokio::process, nix) lives only in adapters and composition; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is normative for layering questions.

scripts/check-architecture.ts is the executable dependency fence (`bun run architecture:check`, first step of `bun run check`): it defines eight per-layer fences (four Rust, four TypeScript) forbidding outward imports by literal string match and throws ArchitectureError listing every violation, so layering changes that cannot pass it are not safe.

The fence's framework-locality pass quarantines platform code to single homes: `#[tauri::command]` only in adapters/inbound/tauri.rs, `generate_handler!`/`.manage(`/`.plugin(` only in composition.rs, and `tokio::process`/`nix::` process primitives only inside adapters/outbound/process.rs and its process/ submodule — while application/ remains allowed tokio::sync primitives.

The Rust application layer owns nine port traits in src-tauri/src/application/ports.rs (EnginePort, TranscriptionPort, ArtifactPort, TranscriptImportPort, RefinementPort, RecordingPort, SettingsPort, plus event ports JobEvents and RecordingEvents), consumed via Arc<dyn Trait> and implemented by outbound adapters.

The frontend port contract BackendPort is owned by the inner layer in src/domain/backend.ts and implemented by TauriBackend in src/adapters/; this placement was a deliberate DIP fix (the contract originally lived in the adapter module, letting ui/ and application/ import an adapter).

Events cross boundaries only through ports: TauriEvents implements both JobEvents and RecordingEvents, wrapping a WorkerEvent plus job_id into the `job-event` channel and RecordingFailure onto `recording-event` (failures map to AppError EVENT_ERROR), while the frontend subscribes via BackendPort.listenToJobs/listenToRecordingFailures whose `() => void` unlistener keeps Tauri's UnlistenFn out of the UI.

The request chain runs TypeScript invoke -> one of 16 Tauri commands (each a thin delegation from State<Application> to a facade method) -> Application facade -> ports -> outbound adapters -> a supervised `python -m galpi_worker` subprocess; events return over the same boundary via job-event/recording-event.

The 16-command IPC surface is registered in one place: composition.rs wires TauriEvents, one DesktopAdapter upcast into five port Arcs, NativeRecorder, and LocalSettingsStore, then registers Application via .manage, loads the dialog/opener plugins, and lists all sixteen commands in generate_handler!.

Each runtime has exactly one composition root: src/main.ts wires the frontend as `new AppController(new TauriBackend(), new AppView(root))` plus start/stop lifecycle; src-tauri/src/composition.rs does all native wiring; worker/galpi_worker/__main__.py dispatches the prepare/transcribe/refine subcommands with an EventWriter injected.

The worker CLI maps requests to a SpeakerHint value object via mutually exclusive `--num-speakers`/`--speaker-range` flags (absent = auto), redirects library stdout to stderr so protocol lines keep stdout, and guarantees every abnormal exit reaches the host as exactly one error event (InvalidInput -> INVALID_INPUT, exit 2; any other exception -> ENGINE_ERROR, exit 1).

The host-worker protocol is versioned JSONL on stdout: one JSON object per line with v/seq/type keys, six event types (phase, log, completed, prepared, refined, error); EventWriter guards a monotonic seq with a threading.Lock so concurrent emitters cannot interleave mid-line, and the Rust domain parser parse_worker_event rejects malformed JSON and unsupported protocol versions.

run_process makes the JSONL protocol safe in practice: the child runs with a cleared env plus explicit allowlist, its own Unix process group, kill_on_drop, and bounded 64 KiB lines (overflow is WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR); stderr is batched 32 lines or 100 ms into single Log events so installs do not flood the webview; a duplicate completed event is a protocol error; and cancellation flushes logs then SIGTERM -> 3s wait -> SIGKILL, always reaping, returning AppError CANCELLED.

The worker protocol is a one-commit change set: worker/galpi_worker/protocol.py ↔ src-tauri/src/domain/worker.rs ↔ src/domain/job.ts (with tauri-backend.ts Zod schemas) ↔ the job-machine reducer must change together; the ASR-context wire format follows the same ownership rule, generated by AsrContext::into_wire_json inside the same Rust domain module as the parser.

The frontend degrades unknown job-event payloads to frontend log lines instead of throwing: toJobEvent maps snake_case wire fields (engine_version -> engineVersion) and converts unrecognized payloads to a log event, because a throw inside Tauri's own listener callback is swallowed and the event would vanish silently, hiding a host/window version mismatch.

TauriBackend is the runtime-validation boundary: every invoke result and both event payloads are parsed with Zod schemas before entering frontend state, per the convention that native responses are never trusted raw.

JobRegistry (application-owned, deliberately not port-hidden) enforces a single active job: a second claim is refused with BUSY, a reused id with JOB_ID_CONFLICT; the returned JobGuard releases the slot on Drop so early returns, cancelled futures, or panics cannot wedge the registry; cancel sends a oneshot exactly once, with ALREADY_CANCELLING and JOB_NOT_FOUND for repeat/unknown attempts.

Recording enforces the same single-slot discipline through a separate active_recording mutex: a second start is RECORDING_BUSY, and stop/cancel verify the recording id, reporting RECORDING_ID_MISMATCH for a different session and RECORDING_NOT_ACTIVE when none is running.

The frontend job lifecycle is a pure immutable reducer: events for a different jobId are ignored, phase events after a settled status are ignored, the log buffer is capped at 200 lines, and cancellation is its own `cancelled` status that a later failJob does not overwrite (the process-death error after a user cancel is a consequence, not a new failure).

The controller subscribes to job-event and recording-event before any IPC operation, and a failed native subscription stops startup with visible Korean copy instead of piling up raw IPC errors — the project convention is to subscribe to Tauri events before invoking the operation that emits them.

Secrets do not round-trip the IPC boundary: the frontend can only ask whether a Hugging Face token is stored (boolean, avoiding a keychain prompt on every settings open), and the assistant API key is read from the keychain only at the moment a refinement actually needs it (ASSISTANT_KEY_MISSING otherwise).

Transcription is gated behind environment readiness at the facade, not the command: Application::transcribe fails with SETUP_REQUIRED when diagnose reports the selected engine not ready, and Qwen3 runs from its own venv with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1/TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 so it loads exclusively from the prepared cache.

The ASR biasing context flows as a private 0600 file: the facade packs saved glossary terms plus participant names/aliases via AsrContext (absent when all lists are empty), the transcription adapter writes it with write_private_file, passes it as `--asr-context`, and removes the file after the run.

Naming conventions split by audience: user-facing copy (command messages, reducer strings, dialog filters, the fallback 예기치 못한 오류가 발생했습니다.) is Korean, while protocol and error identifiers stay stable ASCII; errorMessage surfaces an AppError's Korean message directly and substitutes the stable fallback for anything else, while errorDetail preserves the raw diagnostic for logs.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (dated 2026-08-21) lags current source on counts — it cites 14 commands, 8 port traits, and a four-port DesktopAdapter, while the source now has 16 commands, nine port traits, and five DesktopAdapter impls — so the document is normative for principles and change-set rules while the code and the architecture fence are authoritative for counts and boundaries.

Deliberate non-refactors recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6 must not be 'fixed': one DesktopAdapter implements all five consumer-facing ports (every consumer is the same Application, so splitting only adds composition boilerplate), JobRegistry is not hidden behind a port (in-memory state), BackendPort is one integrated 22-method interface for its single consumer AppController (16 IPC calls, two event subscriptions, four dialog/opener conveniences), and Python has no layer split — its real boundary is purity (core.py, artifacts.py, minutes_*.py are testable without the ML stack).

Verification gates enforce the boundary mechanically: `bun run check` = architecture:check + Biome + tsc --noEmit; `bun run check:all` adds bun test, the Rust gate (cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test), and the worker gate (ruff check/format plus python3 -m unittest discover -s worker/tests -t .), so an architecture violation is always a gate failure rather than a convention that can rot silently.
